title: Outpatient clinic visit
description: Outpatient clinic visit is an appointment with your doctor in a medical office or clinic setting. These visits allow your doctor to assess your health, evaluate symptoms, perform exams, and discuss your medical care. You'll meet with your doctor, who will listen to your concerns and perform appropriate evaluations. Your doctor may order tests, perform physical exams, or discuss treatment options with you. Clinic visits may focus on managing chronic conditions, addressing acute problems, or preventive health maintenance. The complexity of your visit depends on the nature of your health concerns and how much evaluation and discussion is needed. Your doctor will explain findings and discuss next steps in your care during your visit. The cost of this procedure may vary depending on the complexity involved. Categories include low complexity (new or established), moderate complexity (new or established), and high complexity (new or established).

title: Outpatient psychiatric evaluation
description: An outpatient psychiatric evaluation is a comprehensive assessment where a psychiatrist or mental health professional evaluates your mental and emotional health. During this visit, your doctor will ask about your medical history, current symptoms, family history of mental health conditions, and any medications you're taking. They may discuss your mood, sleep patterns, stress levels, and how your symptoms affect daily life. This evaluation helps your doctor diagnose mental health conditions and develop a treatment plan tailored to your needs, which might include therapy, medication, or both.

title: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
description: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a medical treatment where your doctor uses controlled electrical currents to safely trigger a brief seizure under anesthesia. This procedure is typically used when severe depression, bipolar disorder, or catatonia hasn't responded well to medications. The electrical impulses help reset brain chemistry and can provide rapid relief from life-threatening symptoms. You'll be asleep during the procedure and closely monitored by an anesthesiologist. ECT can be very effective, especially when you need quick symptom improvement.

Your therapist uses various evidence-based techniques to help you understand your thoughts and feelings, develop coping strategies, and make positive changes in your life. Psychotherapy can help with depression, anxiety, trauma, relationship issues, and many other concerns. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including group therapy and 1:1 therapy, and the cost may vary depending on the specific approach or service provided.

title: Cardiac electrophysiology study
description: An electrophysiology study maps your heart's electrical system to identify the cause of irregular heartbeats. During this outpatient procedure, your doctor threads thin catheters through blood vessels to your heart while monitoring electrical signals on screens. The test typically lasts 1-3 hours and you're sedated for comfort. This detailed electrical map guides treatment decisions, whether medication adjustments, pacemaker placement, or ablation therapy. Most people go home the same day with minimal restrictions.

This helps diagnose conditions like myocarditis (heart inflammation), cardiomyopathy (heart muscle disease), or transplant rejection. Your doctor uses a special catheter with a tiny biopsy tool guided through your blood vessels into your heart. The procedure is performed in a cardiac catheterization lab while you're awake but sedated. Your doctor can quickly analyze the tissue to determine what's affecting your heart and develop an appropriate treatment plan based on the findings.

Your doctor can see blockages, valve problems, and other abnormalities on X-ray imaging. The procedure is performed while you're awake but sedated, and you'll generally feel minimal discomfort. This detailed information helps your doctor plan the best treatment for your condition, whether that's medication, a stent, bypass surgery, or another intervention.

Your cardiologist uses a catheter to guide the device through your blood vessels into the right ventricle of your heart, where it stays in place. The device monitors your heart rhythm and delivers electrical impulses to keep your heart beating at a healthy rate. This less invasive approach allows you to heal faster.

title: Pacemaker replacement
description: Pacemaker replacement is an outpatient procedure where your doctor removes your old pacemaker and implants a new one. Pacemakers typically last 7-10 years before the battery depletes, at which point replacement is necessary. Your cardiologist makes a small incision under your collarbone, removes the old device, and places a new one in the same location. The wires already in your heart are usually reused and connected to the new device. This procedure helps ensure your pacemaker continues to keep your heart beating at a healthy rate. After recovery, your new device will function just like your previous one.

title: Cardiac rhythm monitor
description: A cardiac rhythm monitor (also called an implantable loop recorder or event monitor) is a small device implanted under your skin to continuously record your heart's electrical activity. This helps your cardiologist diagnose irregular heartbeats (arrhythmias) that may cause fainting, palpitations, or other symptoms. The device stores months of heart rhythm data that your doctor can review at office visits or retrieve remotely. By capturing what's happening with your heart over extended periods, your doctor can diagnose subtle rhythm problems and adjust treatment. This type of procedure can involve removal and insertion of the device, and the cost may vary depending on the specific service performed.

title: Varicose vein treatment
description: Varicose vein treatment closes off swollen, twisted veins in your legs so blood reroutes to healthier veins nearby. Varicose veins form when small valves inside the veins weaken and blood pools, causing bulging, aching, or heaviness. Your doctor performs this in an outpatient clinic using local anesthesia, so you stay awake and go home the same day. Depending on the vein, your doctor may inject a solution that seals it shut or use heat delivered through a thin catheter to close it from the inside. You feel little more than small pinpricks, and the treated veins gradually fade over the following weeks. Most people walk out afterward and return to light activity quickly.

title: Appendectomy
description: Appendectomy is surgery to remove your appendix, a small tube attached to your large intestine. Appendicitis occurs when your appendix becomes inflamed or infected, causing pain and requiring surgical removal to prevent rupture. Your surgeon will carefully remove the inflamed appendix while protecting your other internal organs. This procedure is most often performed urgently or emergently because an inflamed appendix can rupture, causing life-threatening infection. Your surgeon may use either an open approach with a larger incision or a minimally invasive laparoscopic approach with smaller incisions. After appendectomy, you'll recover once your incision heals, usually within 1-2 weeks. You'll receive pain management and instructions about returning to normal activities at your own pace. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including an open surgical approach or a minimally invasive laparoscopic technique, and the cost may vary depending on the method used.

title: Cholecystectomy
description: Cholecystectomy is surgery to remove your gallbladder, a small organ that stores digestive fluid called bile. This surgery is performed when gallstones or other gallbladder problems cause pain or complications. Your surgeon may use either open surgery with a larger incision or laparoscopic surgery with several small incisions. Recovery time varies depending on the surgical approach used. After surgery, you'll gradually return to normal activities as your incisions heal. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including an open surgical approach or a minimally invasive laparoscopic technique, and the cost may vary depending on the method used.

The procedure takes just a few minutes and is performed in your doctor's office or an outpatient clinic. Your doctor uses ultrasound or other imaging to guide the needle to the exact location inside the joint. You may feel pressure or mild discomfort, but the procedure is not very painful. title: Cervical disc replacement
description: A cervical disc replacement is an outpatient surgical procedure where your surgeon removes a damaged disc in your neck and replaces it with an artificial disc that mimics your natural disc's movement. Unlike fusion, which locks vertebrae together, disc replacement preserves motion in your neck. The surgery is performed from the front of your neck and usually takes 1-2 hours. You may go home the same day or stay overnight depending on your surgeon's preference and your condition. You'll wear a neck brace temporarily to support healing. Recovery typically takes 6-12 weeks, and you can often return to normal activities within this timeframe. Physical therapy helps restore strength and motion. The goal is to relieve your pain while maintaining better neck flexibility than fusion would provide. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including removal/replacement and total, and the cost may vary depending on the extent of the procedure.

description: Non-surgical ankle fracture treatment is an outpatient procedure where your doctor treats your broken ankle without surgery by immobilizing it with a cast or boot. Your doctor will first take X-rays to determine the type and location of your fracture. If the break is stable and the bone pieces are properly aligned, surgery is not necessary. Your doctor will apply a cast or walking boot to keep the ankle immobilized so the bone can heal. You'll need to keep weight off your ankle for several weeks, using crutches or a walker. X-rays will be taken periodically to monitor healing progress. Physical therapy helps restore your strength and motion once healing is underway. Your ankle will be tender for several weeks, and full healing typically takes 6-12 weeks depending on the fracture severity. The cost of this procedure may vary depending on whether your doctor needs to manually reposition (manipulate) the bone fragments into proper alignment, or whether the fracture can heal in its current position without manipulation.

description: A trigger point injection is an outpatient procedure where your doctor injects medication directly into a trigger point, a tight, knotted muscle that's causing pain. description: Pathology testing where a tissue sample is removed and examined under a microscope in a laboratory to diagnose diseases, especially cancer. A pathologist (a doctor specializing in examining tissues) analyzes your sample at different levels of detail and complexity. Pathologists examine the cells to determine if cancer or other disease is present and to understand the severity and characteristics of any disease found. Different levels of testing range from simple examination to highly complex analysis using special stains and genetic testing. Results guide your treatment decisions and doctors' understanding of your condition. Four different complexity levels of testing exist depending on what information your doctor needs. Results help your doctor understand what's happening during your sleep and determine the right treatment for you. You'll receive a detailed report showing your sleep patterns and any interruptions. The scanner detects the tracer's signals to show your doctor blood flow and heart function. This test helps identify areas of poor blood flow or damaged heart tissue. There's minimal radiation exposure, and most people return home the same day with no recovery time needed.

description: An arteriovenous (AV) access is a surgically created connection between an artery and vein in your arm or leg that allows blood to flow quickly for dialysis treatment. During this procedure, your surgeon connects a vein directly to an artery, which causes the vein to enlarge and strengthen over time. This enlarged vein provides reliable access for dialysis needles and improves blood flow during treatment. The procedure takes about an hour and is typically performed as an outpatient surgery. You'll receive local or regional anesthesia so you remain awake but comfortable. Recovery usually takes a few days, though the access may need 2-6 weeks to fully mature before it's ready for dialysis. This procedure can be done as a simple connection or a more complex revision if you have scar tissue or need repair of an existing access. The cost of this procedure may vary depending on the complexity involved. Categories include arteriovenous (av) anastomosis, simple and complex (incl. revision or repair).

title: Dialysis
description: Dialysis is a lifesaving treatment that removes waste and excess water from your blood when your kidneys can no longer do this job. Two main types exist: hemodialysis (filtering blood through an artificial kidney machine) and peritoneal dialysis (using your abdominal lining to filter blood). The type of dialysis recommended depends on your kidney function level, lifestyle, and medical status. Most dialysis patients require three sessions per week, each lasting 3-5 hours. With proper dialysis and medical management, patients with kidney failure can enjoy good quality of life.

title: Eye exam
description: An eye exam is a comprehensive check of your vision and the health of your eyes. Your eye doctor measures how clearly you see, determines whether you need glasses or contact lenses, and examines the structures inside and outside your eyes for signs of disease. During the visit you read from an eye chart, look through different lenses to fine-tune your prescription, and have the pressure and interior of your eyes checked, sometimes after drops are used to widen your pupils. The exam is painless, though dilating drops can make your vision blurry and light-sensitive for a few hours. Regular eye exams keep your prescription current and help catch conditions such as glaucoma, cataracts, or diabetic eye changes early, when they are most treatable.

title: Cataract surgery
description: Cataract surgery is an outpatient procedure that removes your cloudy lens and replaces it with a clear artificial lens to restore vision. Your eye surgeon makes a small incision, breaks up the cloudy lens with ultrasound, and gently removes it. A new lens implant is inserted to focus light on your retina. The procedure takes about 15 minutes per eye under local anesthesia. You go home the same day and vision gradually improves over weeks. This category includes standard extraction and extraction combined with glaucoma treatment (MIGS, Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery). This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including standard extraction and with migs, and the cost may vary depending on the approach used.

title: Retinal repair surgery
description: Retinal repair surgery is an outpatient procedure that repairs damage to your retina, such as a retinal detachment, hole, or macular problem. Your ophthalmologist performs specialized techniques to reattach the retina or repair the damage using lasers, injected gases, or oils. The procedure takes 1-3 hours depending on the problem. You go home the same day or may stay overnight. Recovery involves activity restrictions, positioning requirements, and frequent follow-up appointments to monitor healing.

title: Glaucoma surgery
description: Glaucoma surgery lowers the pressure inside the eye (intraocular pressure) when eye drops, oral medications, or laser treatment have not been sufficient to prevent progressive damage to the optic nerve. Several surgical approaches are used depending on the type and severity of glaucoma: trabeculectomy creates a new drainage opening in the eye wall; canaloplasty uses a microcatheter and stent to widen the eye's natural drainage canal; and aqueous shunt implantation (tube shunt surgery) places a small drainage device to redirect fluid to a reservoir under the conjunctiva. Your ophthalmologist will recommend the most appropriate procedure based on your specific diagnosis, prior treatments, and overall eye health. The goal in all cases is to stabilize eye pressure and protect your remaining vision.

title: YAG laser capsulotomy
description: A YAG (yttrium-aluminum-garnet) laser capsulotomy is a quick laser procedure that restores clear vision when the membrane behind a lens implant becomes cloudy after cataract surgery. This clouding, sometimes called a secondary cataract, can develop months or years later and cause blurry or hazy vision much like the original cataract. Your eye doctor uses numbing drops and a focused laser to create a small opening in the cloudy membrane, letting light pass through clearly again. You sit at a machine and see flashes of light, and most people feel little or no discomfort. The procedure takes only a few minutes, requires no incision, and most people notice their vision clear within a day, returning to normal activities almost immediately.
